summary: Upgrades the login library better-auth from 1.6 to 1.7.14 and adds a nullable session.impersonatedBy column (migration) because 1.7 checks the schema at startup and blocks every /api/auth request if a column its plugins (here the admin plugin in lib/auth.ts) write is missing; adds a docs note.

statements.why: Additive nullable column plus a dependency upgrade; no data loss or access change in the code. The risk (migration must be applied) is covered by the steps.

statements.text: Sessions now also store the impersonated by.
statements.why: prisma/schema.prisma Session.impersonatedBy String? + migration ALTER TABLE "session" ADD COLUMN "impersonatedBy" TEXT.
Adds a developer note that better-auth 1.7 fails every /api/auth/* request when a plugin column is missing; the card doesn't relay it.

statements.text: Apply prisma/migrations/20261029000000_session_impersonated_by to your live database before the new code goes live, or the parts that use it will fail.
statements.why: Correct to apply first, but understated: per the commit and docs note, without the column better-auth 1.7 fails every /api/auth/* request, so nobody can sign in, not just 'the parts that use it'.

statements.text: Test anything that uses better-auth: it was upgraded from ^1.6.22 to ^1.7.14.
statements.why: package.json bump (lockfile 1.6.25 -> 1.7.14); better-auth handles all login/sessions, so sign-in, OTP email and admin flows should be tested.

statements.text: (Hidden: 1 file with only formatting changes, or lockfiles.)
statements.why: pnpm-lock.yaml for the better-auth upgrade; 4 shown + 1 hidden = the commit's 5 files.

misses.what: better-auth is the login system for the whole app; if the new code deploys before the migration runs, every sign-in/session request fails ('Prisma schema mismatch').
